subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should OpenClaw support `bindings[].tools.allow/deny` as an enforceable core security boundary for route and ACP bindings, or should operators use existing group/sender/session policy surfaces instead?
rationale: This would add a new config and authorization boundary across route matching, ACP bindings, Gateway tool resolution, embedded-agent tool construction, and existing policy precedence; automation cannot safely choose that product/security contract.

options.title: Design binding-scoped policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and regression proof before implementation.

options.title: Use existing policy surfaces
options.body: Decline the new binding key and document group/channel, sender, session, and per-agent policy as the supported way to restrict tools.

options.title: Defer to broader identity/session work
options.body: Leave this blocked on scoped session or conversation identity design if maintainers want one authorization model instead of a binding-specific slice.

recommendation.title: Design binding-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and regression proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across scoped conversation profiles and tool-policy pipeline ownership adjacent to this decision.
